description: Lets the real CI-Server web app (served remotely at http://127.0.0.1:8642 / http://localhost:8642 after the bootstrap page's window.location.replace()) keep its device key in the OS keychain without ever reading it back. It writes and removes keychain entries with tauri-plugin-ci-auth's secure_set and secure_remove (the key once, right after it mints it at sign-in; everything at sign-out). It reads them only through this app's device_secure_get_command, which returns every entry except the device key itself (memory:ci.apiKey reads as absent), and it gets short-lived access tokens for the key from device_access_token_command, which asks Memory at the fixed gateway address and keeps the key in Rust (src-tauri/src/device_key.rs). The plugin's own secure_get, its loopback sign-in commands and its `ci-auth:default` set are deliberately not granted. The web side namespaces every key it stores (`memory:` in @ci/common's nativeBridge.ts).
